column1: # Run 3 · Stage 6 · the retro-discrimination census. One line per row, TAB separated:
# The row set is generated from the run's own test sources by `scripts/extract_rows.py`, so it
# equals the tree's row set by construction. `scripts/s6_census.sh` re-derives every bucket and
# fails if this file and the tree disagree.
# ANCHOR         the row reads differently at one of the four anchors, so a compiler from before
#                the run fails it. the witness names which anchors.
# PREFIX         it agrees with every anchor but differs at a run-internal prefix, so it
#                discriminates a commit this run made.
# CTRL-ABLATION  it agrees everywhere in history AND moves when a named rule is deleted.
# CTRL-NOSTORE   it reaches managed memory but forms no element address, so no rule this run
#                wrote can move it. the witness says why, per row.
# CTRL-INERT     accepted at allocs=0: it reaches no managed memory at all.
# CTRL-FENCE     refused. it pins a fence rather than a value.
# The last four buckets are controls, not claims. A control that started discriminating would be
# a rule change nobody declared, which is why they are pinned here rather than left implicit.
